proposals.before: Lingchi applied to the gravest offenses among the Ten Abominations—unfilial conduct and worse—and was regarded as the supreme penalty.
proposals.after: Lingchi applied to the gravest offenses among the Ten Abominations—crimes of inhumanity (budao) and above—and was regarded as the supreme penalty.
proposals.reason: 不道 is the Ten Abominations category of inhuman/unnatural crimes, not unfilial conduct (不孝).

proposals.before: Lingchi was applied to such grave offenses among the Ten Abominations as unfilial conduct and above, and was called the extreme punishment.
proposals.after: Lingchi was applied to such grave offenses among the Ten Abominations as inhumanity (budao) and above, and was called the extreme punishment.
proposals.reason: 不道 should not be rendered as unfilial conduct; that sense belongs to 不孝.

proposals.before: From Jin onward families could still share punishment, but Tang law limited guilt by association to rebellion, felonious sons, and unfilial conduct alone.
proposals.after: From Jin onward families could still share punishment, but Tang law limited guilt by association to rebellion, felonious contumacy against parents or grandparents (e'ni), and crimes of inhumanity (budao) alone.
proposals.reason: 惡逆 and 不道 are distinct Ten Abominations categories; 不道 is not unfilial conduct.

proposals.before: From Jin onward there remained laws for family members to share punishment; in the Tang Code only rebellion, felonious sons, and unfilial conduct had guilt by association in the code—nothing else did.
proposals.after: From Jin onward there remained laws for family members to share punishment; in the Tang Code only rebellion, felonious contumacy (e'ni), and inhumanity (budao) had guilt by association in the code—nothing else did.
proposals.reason: 不道 is mistranslated as unfilial conduct; 惡逆 is better as felonious contumacy than only felonious sons.

decisions.reason: s0110 has 十惡中不道以上: 不道 is the Ten Abominations category of inhumanity, distinct from 不孝 (unfilial conduct). The prior idiomatic wrongly renders 不道 as unfilial conduct; the proposed replacement restores the correct category and keeps the rest of the sentence.
The same phrase 不道以上 must not be read as unfilial conduct. The prior literal conflates 不道 with 不孝; rendering it as inhumanity (budao) and above matches the Chinese.

s0160 lists Tang guilt-by-association as 反叛、惡逆、不道—three distinct categories. The prior idiomatic turns 惡逆 into 'felonious sons' and 不道 into 'unfilial conduct' (不孝); the proposed e'ni and budao wording corrects both names without changing the sentence structure.

The literal must track the same triad 反叛、惡逆、不道. Replacing 'felonious sons' and 'unfilial conduct' with felonious contumacy (e'ni) and inhumanity (budao) restores the Ten Abominations terms named in the Chinese.
